part: Number, ages and activities of the children

part: Three briefs per parent (evening 19:30, Sunday 18:00, weekday 07:00): six jobs, with the times written into the card's name

challenge_note: Merges the over-engineering finding on six jobs with the assumption finding on send times; no roadmap line, source or dependent card needs three briefs, so it stands.

part: Household-store read on the week-ahead and morning legs (items due, trash day, open school deadlines), fed by school-deadline rows that F010 stores

loses: An 'items due' line fed from store rows. If the notification policy is not built, a pause is Tony disabling the job.

part: Email-derived dates fed into the week-ahead from a separate mail-agent job using llm-task, still labelled 'G015, wave C'

part: The [T]/[S] driver tag on calendar events and the per-child routines-and-gear table

part: Part 2, the calendar write: an in-house write server around gog, its own write token, an approval hook, attendee stripping

part: Second calendar route: a plugin that sends a tap-to-add calendar file

loses: nothing
challenge_note: Narrowed: the card already gates the plugin on a phone test, so what survives is the order, with the hand test run first because a pass removes the expensive write route for good; it agrees with the deferral in the row above.

part: Re-opening iMessage groups for a parents' chat with a new group agent, placed in wave A as 'ready now'
problem: The card adds a new shared agent and reverses something Tony signed off at M1 (iMessage groups disabled) so that Happy can answer weather and web questions in a three-way chat. loses: nothing (two texts, one per phone, instead of one group text)
challenge_note: The roadmap's Replies row (line 150) already requires per-owner delivery, so the simpler design is the plan of record; I removed the reviewer's side suggestion of a job that posts to the group's chat id, which would cut against the same row.

part: Storm-alert watcher: a script polling every 30 minutes round the clock, with id dedup, an urgent class that passes quiet hours, and a promised chore checklist

Card caveats 2 and 10, unverified items 1 and 3, source support.apple.com/en-us/102516. Fact sheet: quiet hours never stated; Tony's own example of a monitor was school email. CRT-04 names the weather watch as a job that still works while the model is down, but does not depend on it.

proposal.text: No storm script in the first build. Add one sentence to the evening brief: when an alert is active, name it and, on a school night, say to watch for the school's own notice. Each parent switches on severe-weather notifications in the Weather app. If Tony wants the watcher anyway: daytime runs only, alert types he picks, and no chore list unless he writes one. Taken with the two rows below, F018 then has nothing left to build in wave B.

loses: A text from Happy at the moment an alert is issued, and any alert text on Friday and Saturday evenings, when no brief runs. The phone covers this only if the Weather app's notifications are on, and which alert types those cover is unverified on the card. CRT-04 loses its example of an alert that needs no model.
challenge_note: Merges the drop finding with the night-text and chore-checklist findings; I confirmed in nws.js that alerts already ride on every forecast and found no dependent card, and made the stated loss fuller (weekends, phone coverage unverified).

part: Recall watch: two scripts (CPSC daily, FDA twice a day) matched against four family keyword lists in family.json5
problem: The match depends on lists of what the family owns, eats and takes, including allergens and medicines, that do not exist and that someone would have to write and keep current. Nobody has said the family has allergies or regular medicines. The card says substring matching gives false alarms and misses, and that both agencies offer their own sign-ups.
checked: Card caveats 2, 8 and 9, depends_on last line, and its CPSC and FDA subscription sources. Fact sheet: allergies and medications never stated; whole-inbox reading moved to wave B. Config repo family.json5, keys only: no such lists. G015 description: a 07:00 digest of each parent's inbox.

proposal.text: No recall scripts and no keyword lists. A parent who wants recall news signs up for the agencies' own emails, which then pass through the 07:00 mail digest like any other mail. Revisit only if Tony says he would write and keep the lists.

loses: Any match against what the family owns: the agencies' emails are unfiltered, and the mail agent does not know what is in the house.
challenge_note: Merges the drop and keyword-list findings; I removed the reviewer's 'mention a recall that looks relevant' sentence for the digest, because the mail agent holds no list of what the family owns to judge relevance by.

part: Team-schedule watcher (hourly) and generic changed-page watcher (every 6 hours)
problem: Two general-purpose scripts are planned before anyone has named a team feed or a page to watch. Tony has not said the children are on a team, the card says the team app's own push is faster and that a hash watch fires on changes that do not matter, and the first check of which sites even publish a feed is still outstanding.
checked: Card caveats 2 and 7, unverified items 4 and 6 to 8, depends_on line 5. Fact sheet: activities, teams and school platforms never stated. Card sources: the three team apps document subscribing their schedule into a calendar, which F009 then reads. CRT-11 is the only card that uses the page watch (camp registration), and its default above is 'later'.

proposal.text: Write neither script now. When a parent names one feed or page: subscribe a team schedule into the family calendar first (no code), and write one script for that one page only if that is not enough.

loses: Nothing today; later, a 'game moved' text for a same-day change, which the team app's own push covers.
challenge_note: Merges the defer finding with the team-app assumption; the only dependent is CRT-11's registration watch, which waits with that card, so nothing requires the scripts now.

part: Each script checks every address itself (https, public host)
problem: A general address checker is asked of scripts that fetch only addresses Tony registered, show the result to no model and print a fixed line. The existing weather plugin handles the same concern by pinning one host.
checked: Card caveat 5 and safety. F083 how ('keep the api.weather.gov host pin'). Roadmap line 414: outbound HTTPS goes through an egress proxy that blocks private addresses; card caveat 5: command jobs run outside that proxy, the sandbox and OpenClaw's fetch guardrails.

proposal.text: Each script is pinned to its one registered host and refuses redirects to any other host. No general public-address checker.

loses: The refusal of a registered name that resolves to an address on the home network.
challenge_note: Overturned: command jobs bypass the egress proxy that blocks private addresses (roadmap line 414), so the script-side check stands in for a roadmap rule; it is a few lines, a host pin alone does not replace it, and the point is moot if the scripts are deferred.

part: Workarounds for the notification policy's 'dropped, not sent later' rule, repeated in four cards
problem: Because the planned policy drops a text instead of holding it, four cards each add their own fix: run only inside allowed hours, an urgent class for storms, a loss 'written into each job's charter', an extra store read on the brief, and limits on what may go to the group. Tony never asked for quiet hours or a daily cap, and with the defaults above a parent gets about three scheduled texts on a weekday.
checked: F018 caveat 10 and depends_on line 2, MKT-06 caveat 5, F014 caveat 8, F006 caveat 5; G001 description and caveats 1, 2 and 11. Fact sheet: quiet hours, preferred times and a daily cap never stated. Roadmap text: no mention of quiet hours, a cap or a notification policy.

proposal.text: Do you want a daily cap and quiet hours enforced by a plugin in the first build? Default if no answer: no. Every scheduled job gets a daytime hour in its schedule line, and the policy is revisited only if the texts turn out to be too many. The four cards then lose these workarounds and their dependency on G001. (G001 itself is reviewed in its own part of the catalog; this row is about what it costs these four cards.)

loses: An enforced cap and a mute by chat; a pause is Tony disabling a job, and each phone's own night-time silencing still works.
challenge_note: Checked the roadmap and the fact sheet for any quiet-hours or cap requirement and found none; the workarounds exist only because of G001's drop rule, so the finding stands as a question about whether that policy is wanted first.
